text: The core lesson Searle draws from the Chinese Room is that:
choices: Computers can never pass the Turing test
The person in the room genuinely understands Chinese after all
Syntactic symbol manipulation (running the right program) is not sufficient for semantics/understanding
explanation: Searle's Chinese Room is meant to show that running the right program - pure syntactic symbol manipulation - is not sufficient for semantics/understanding. Option 1 contradicts the argument (the man precisely does not understand), option 0 misstates it as a claim about the Turing test, and option 2 attributes to Searle a dualism he rejects (he holds understanding requires biological causal powers, not a soul).
